description:
Celestial is a technology-driven team participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. We aim to combine software development, creative thinking, and space science to build an engaging solution for the Space Mission Design Game.

We value experimentation, collaboration, and practical problem-solving. We welcome teammates interested in programming, game development, UI/UX, 3D modelling, animation, astrophysics, and space exploration.
summary:
ODIUM: Grand Prix of the Solar System is an interactive, browser-based space mission design game built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Players step into the role of a mission director under a strict budget cap, designing an interplanetary probe across real aerospace trade-offs—propulsion architectures, launcher payload capacities, solar flux inverse-square decay, eclipse battery reserves, and deep-space Friis comms bandwidth.

Rather than calculating in isolation, PODIUM pits the player against two distinct AI rival agencies—cautious, over-margined Helios Dynamics and aggressive, high-risk Vanta Aerospace—launching on the same day in a race across interplanetary space. With switchable 3D orbital cameras, live F1-style timing towers, mid-flight pit-wall decision calls, and an interactive telemetry flight recorder, players see firsthand how an early aggressive burn or an under-sized battery directly impacts mission survival and arrival order.

By framing authentic orbital mechanics (Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, power margins, and radiation faults) through high-stakes competitive racing and a 3-step podium ceremony, PODIUM demystifies mission design engineering, transforming complex multidisciplinary tradeoffs into an accessible, intuitive, and unforgettable educational experience.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

PODIUM is a browser-based aerospace trade-off game that reframes interplanetary mission design as a high-stakes Grand Prix. Players design a spacecraft under a strict budget cap to reach destinations like Mars or Europa, balancing propulsion architectures, wet mass, power generation, battery eclipse reserves, deep-space comms, and redundancy. Instead of calculating in isolation, the player launches alongside two deterministic AI rivals: cautious Helios Dynamics and aggressive Vanta Aerospace. The mission unfolds in real-time through an interactive 3D WebGL scene featuring an F1-style live Timing Tower, dynamic mid-flight Pit-Wall decision prompts, an interactive Flight Recorder telemetry chart, and a 3-step podium awards ceremony.

What benefits does it have and what is the intended impact?

PODIUM makes complex aerospace systems engineering intuitive. Adding a heavier instrument increases dry mass, which exponentially multiplies propellant requirements via the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, forcing a costlier launcher that threatens the budget cap. Instead of generic failure screens, the game provides transparent root-cause analysis chains explaining the exact engineering fault behind every delay or anomaly. By combining real orbital mechanics with the drama of motorsport, PODIUM turns intimidating equations into an engaging, accessible STEM learning experience.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

PODIUM was built with TypeScript, React 18, and Vite for a fast, responsive user interface. The 3D planetary orbits and racing spacecraft are rendered with Three.js and React Three Fiber. Interface styling and motion use Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, Lucide Icons, and Canvas Confetti. Headless automated test suites were built with Vitest to rigorously verify rocket equations, inverse-square solar decay, and rival AI generation. The client-side application is deployed globally on the Vercel Edge Network.

How is your project creative?

PODIUM blends authentic orbital physics with motorsport race culture. Trajectory correction burns act as Pit Stops; radiation safe modes act as Safety Cars; coronal mass ejections act as Adverse Weather; and interplanetary transit choices mirror Sprint versus Endurance fuel strategies. Live interval gaps, animated timing tower position swaps, tactical auto-pausing pit-wall calls, and distinct AI rival personalities transform a technical engineering simulator into a gripping competitive spectacle.

What factors did your team consider?

Our team prioritized scientific rigor, implementing real mathematical formulas for Tsiolkovsky delta-V, inverse-square solar flux attenuation (explaining why solar works at Mars but requires nuclear RTGs at Europa), 70% battery depth-of-discharge limits during shadow passes, and Friis comms downlink bandwidth scaling. We also built in deterministic reproducibility using a 32-bit mulberry32 pseudo-random number generator for identical daily challenge seeds, alongside accessibility support for reduced motion, bloom toggles, and high-contrast telemetry dials.
